# CMF-true-stereo **Real left/right stereo on the CMF Phone 1.** The earpiece becomes the left speaker, the bottom speaker the right — no custom kernel, just root.

Download the module · Get the app · How stereo works

| | | |---|---| | 🔊 **Stereo** | Earpiece = left, speaker = right. Games, films and music finally have sides. | | 📢 **Mono** | Default. Both speakers play the full mix: louder and fuller than the bottom speaker alone. | | 📱 **App** | *CMF Stereo*, a clean Nothing-style app: on/off, Mono/Stereo, two 1–10 levels. | | 🛟 **Safe** | Patches nothing it has not verified, never touches the vendor partition, and undoes itself after two failed boots. | ### Install in three steps 1. Flash the zip in **Magisk / KernelSU / APatch** and reboot. 2. Open **CMF Stereo** and pick **Stereo** — or in a terminal: `su -c stereoctl channels stereo`. It switches at once (the sound stops for a moment; press play again). 3. Turn the phone sideways either way: left and right follow the screen. Works on the **CMF Phone 1 (A015)**. On any other phone it installs and does nothing. > **Before you use stereo** > - Stereo turns off Awinic's speaker protection for media (calls always keep > it). To make up for it, the speaker is held **6 dB below the amp's full > output** at its loudest (app speaker level 10), and each level down takes > 2 dB more, to 24 dB at level 1. Use **Mono** for loud listening. > - If the phone fails to boot twice in a row with stereo on, the module > removes stereo on its own and falls back to Mono. > > Details in [Mono and stereo](#mono-and-stereo). ## Status **Current release: v0.9.7** (CMF Phone 1, Nothing OS B4.1, Android 16). Stereo works and is in daily use on the test phone. Mono and Stereo switch without a reboot, left and right follow the phone's orientation, and Magisk offers new releases as updates. **Verified on the phone** - Magisk's Update button: with v0.9.6 installed, Magisk showed **Update** for this module once v0.9.7 was out and `update.json` named it (before that it rightly showed none). - v0.9.5 orientation swap: the left-only test file in VLC (deep-buffer output) and in USB Audio Player Pro (primary output, where Nothing's Dirac does the swap): earpiece on your left, the earpiece plays; on your right, the speaker plays. The first build cancelled Dirac's own swap on the primary output; diagnostic builds found it, and the patch now leaves that output to Dirac. - v0.9.4 live switching: Mono -> Stereo -> Mono -> Stereo with `stereoctl channels`, no reboot, each checked with the left-only test file (speaker silent in Stereo, both play in Mono). The first two builds refused it safely (no stock copy; then mounting over the deleted files Magisk had mounted), which is what the final design fixed. - v0.9.4 kernel log: boot messages intact, one `aw882xx_volume_put` at boot instead of a `volume_get` line every cycle. - Stereo: a left-only test file leaves the speaker silent on its right slot and plays on the earpiece, with Nothing's Dirac tuning on and off. - Mono and stereo switching through `stereoctl channels` and the app, with a reboot. - Restarting the audio HAL by hand (`setprop ctl.restart vendor.audio-hal`) while playing: the HAL came back, players paused, calls worked. - One daemon per boot (three were starting before v0.9.1). - Earpiece at +8 dB (`Handset Volume 0`) while playing; the old 31 is corrected on install. - Hi-res playback (USB Audio Player Pro, Direct 192 kHz) still works in stereo. **Not tested on a phone yet** - v0.9.7 author after updating: Magisk should list the module as by Dr.Essence (was Tiimoo-debug); the published zip's `module.prop` was checked. - Installing an update from Magisk's Update button and rebooting (button seen; install not reported yet). - The orientation swap with Nothing's Dirac switched off: apps on the primary output are then not swapped (known limit; nothing swaps them). - Live switching from the app's Mono/Stereo buttons (needs the next app build). - v0.9.3: on/off speed and the lighter daemon. Passes the test suite under mksh (Android's shell), dash and busybox; needs a check on the phone: `time su -c stereoctl off`, then `time su -c stereoctl on`, and the earpiece still engaging when audio starts. - The boot watchdog removing the stereo overlay after two failed boots (no failed boot has happened to trigger it). - Re-staging stereo during a module update, and the refusal on a different Nothing OS build (needs the next OTA). - How the speaker holds up to long, loud stereo listening without Awinic's protection. **Pending** - Hardware checked (I2C devices, driver bindings, mixer, HAL): one Awinic amp at `6-0034` (mono output, speaker only); the earpiece is on the codec's left DAC, which takes only channel 1; the codec's earpiece amp is at its top step (+8 dB) and the digital path has about 0.3 dB left. Ideas under consideration: an earpiece boost (high-pass, compressor and limiter on the earpiece channel through Android's DynamicsProcessing, in the app), and a mono speaker fallback when the phone is turned with the earpiece on the right (a true left/right swap would need the channels swapped in the stream: a bigger project). - Which stereo speaker level sounds as loud as stock (Mono, with Awinic's protection): needs a by-ear comparison on the phone, level by level, with the same track. - A short clip of the earpiece and speaker splitting a game's or film's audio, for the README and the release page. - Check the vendor file hashes after the next Nothing OS update and add the new build. - `ADDA_DL_MAX_VOL` was tried for a louder earpiece: no clear difference, left out. **Fixed recently** - v0.9.7: the module was still listed in Magisk as by Tiimoo-debug; it now says Dr.Essence. - v0.9.6: Magisk showed an out-of-date module description (Stereo "needs a reboot"). - v0.9.5: turned with the earpiece on your right, left and right came out reversed. - v0.9.4: switching Mono and Stereo needed a reboot; it now restarts only the audio HAL. From a stereo boot, the stock files are rebuilt from the stereo ones (original bytes back, then hash-checked), so mono can be switched to live without ever having booted mono. - v0.9.4: the daemon read the amp's volume every cycle, and the Awinic driver logs each read, so dmesg filled with `aw882xx_volume_get` lines (about 20 a minute) and lost the boot messages. - v0.9.3: every mixer read started tinymix three times and every write five (its style check was cached inside a subshell and thrown away), on every 2 s daemon cycle. It is now detected once per process. - v0.9.3: on/off waited on fixed sleeps: up to 2 s for the daemon to notice the stop, 1 s polling for it to exit, and a flat 2 s after restarting it. The daemon now stops the moment it is told to and both waits poll in tenths of a second. - v0.9.3: finding the daemon started two programs for every process on the phone (several hundred), at least twice per on/off. It now checks only shells and the daemon itself. Measured in a test container with a running daemon: `on` 0.05 s, `off` 0.18 s. - v0.9.3: `stereoctl status brief` for the app, without reading every control back. - v0.9.2: earpiece gain was 31 (the codec's mute value), not the maximum. - v0.9.1: three daemons fought over the mixer; `status` reported "not running". - v0.9.0: true stereo: the HAL and Awinic DSP mono folds switched off in stereo mode. --- ## About A Magisk / KernelSU / APatch module that makes the **CMF Phone 1** play media out of its **earpiece as well as its bottom speaker** — in true stereo if you want it. It has two channel modes: - **mono** (default, stock audio): both drivers play the same full mix — louder, fuller and taller than the single bottom-firing speaker. This was the whole module once, back when it was called cmf-fake-stereo. - **stereo**: real left/right. The **earpiece plays the left channel and the speaker the right**. It costs Awinic's speaker-protection processing on media, so the speaker amp is held at a fixed attenuation instead. See [Mono and stereo](#mono-and-stereo). Getting stereo took finding the two places the phone folds the speaker to mono; the [Findings](#findings-what-this-device-actually-does) section shows the measurements rather than asking you to take my word. Verified on **A015 / Tetris, MT6878, Nothing OS B4.1, Android 16.** ## What it does - **Real stereo** in stereo mode: earpiece = left channel, bottom speaker = right - **Mono** mode: both speakers play the full mix, with full speaker protection - Plays media through the earpiece alongside the speaker, automatically - Earpiece at the receiver amp's maximum, +8 dB (`Handset Volume 0`), the same value the HAL uses - Applies only while audio is playing, so the receiver is not held energised - Steps aside for headphones and Bluetooth - Restores every control it touches on stop, disarm or uninstall - Disarms itself if it ever causes a failed boot - Switch modes with `stereoctl channels mono|stereo` or the app; the stereo overlay removes itself after two failed boots ## What it does not do - **No speaker protection on media in stereo.** Awinic's DSP processing is the part that folds to mono, so stereo replaces it (see [Mono and stereo](#mono-and-stereo)). - **No extra volume from the main speaker.** It is untouched. - **Nothing on other devices out of the box.** It installs inert elsewhere and ships a probe to work out that device's routing. ## Quick start Flash the zip (build it with `./build.sh`, or grab a release), reboot, play something. That is the whole setup on a CMF Phone 1 — the verified routing is preconfigured. To check it is working, with audio playing: ```sh su stereoctl status # all three controls should show want= matching now= stereoctl solo # speaker off, earpiece only - proves it is really the earpiece stereoctl unsolo ``` For real stereo (applied at once): ```sh su -c stereoctl channels stereo ``` If it is ever silent, `stereoctl doctor` walks every layer that can cause that and names the one responsible. ## On other devices It installs with an empty `actions.conf` and changes nothing. Run `stereoctl probe` to dump the audio hardware — ALSA topology, every mixer control, smart-amp drivers, HAL configs and MediaTek's AudioParam tree — then `stereoctl report` to fold it into one shareable text file. The routing for that device gets written into `actions.conf` from what the probe finds. See [Why it ships empty elsewhere](#why-it-ships-empty-elsewhere). --- ## How it works Three layers, smallest hammer first. **1. Mixer actions (`actions.conf`).** The real work. An ALSA mixer control somewhere enables the receiver output stage; on MediaTek there is usually also a routing control that decides which DL (downlink) stream feeds it. Setting those while the speaker is playing is what puts the earpiece to work next to the speaker. The audio HAL rewrites mixer controls on every route change, so a one-shot write does not survive the next stream start. A small daemon re-asserts the values every couple of seconds and — by default — only while audio is actually playing, so the earpiece is not left energised all day. Everything touched has its original value saved under `/data/adb/cmf-stereo/state/` and restored on stop, disarm or uninstall. **2. Audio policy overlay (`stereoctl xml-patch`, optional).** If the policy declares the speaker as `AUDIO_CHANNEL_OUT_MONO`, the framework downmixes to one channel before the HAL ever sees it, and no amount of mixer work brings the second channel back. The patch widens only the speaker `` to stereo, in an overlay copy — the vendor partition is never written. It is opt-in, validated before it is installed, and reversible. **3. What the CMF Phone 1 actually needed.** Worth recording, because it was not any of the obvious answers and the probe is what found it. Media on this device never touches the internal codec. Playback runs: ``` DL_24CH_CH1/CH2 ──▶ I2SOUT4_CH1/CH2 ──▶ Awinic aw_dev_0 smart PA ──▶ speaker ◀── I2SIN4 ──▶ UL3 (IV-sense feedback) ``` The earpiece hangs off the internal codec's DAC (`ADDA_DL`), and that DAC normally has **no source connected at all** — every one of its ~20 input switches sits Off. So pointing `RCV Mux` at the receiver routes it to a silent wire, which is exactly what happened on the first attempt. The switch that matters is `ADDA_DL_CH1 DL_24CH_CH1`: it feeds the internal DAC from the same `DL_24CH` stream already going to the speaker amp. Turn it on, then open `RCV Mux`, and the earpiece plays. There is only one Awinic device (`aw_dev_0`), so there is no second amp channel to press into service — the internal codec was the only way in. That alone gives both drivers the same full mix: **mono mode**. Real stereo needed one more step — switching off the two places the phone folds the speaker to mono — which is what `stereoctl channels stereo` adds (see [Findings](#findings-what-this-device-actually-does) and [Mono and stereo](#mono-and-stereo)). ## Findings: what this device actually does ### Where the speaker is folded to mono Earlier revisions of this section said both transducers were hard-wired to channel 1, then that a custom kernel would be needed, then that the DSP firmware was the limit. All three were wrong. Each stage was measured with a test file that has sound on the left channel only and silence on the right, by switching the amp to its right slot: silence there means the right channel really is separate. | Stage | Separate L/R? | Evidence | |---|---|---| | Android framework | Yes | `dumpsys media.audio_flinger`: speaker output is 2-channel FL/FR, *Master mono* off. The policy's speaker port is already stereo, so `stereoctl xml-patch` finds nothing to change. | | Dirac (Nothing's speaker tuning) | Not the fold | Session-0 insert effect, 2-in/2-out presets. Removing it alone changed nothing. | | MediaTek audio HAL (`audio.primary.mt6878.so`) | **Folds to mono** | `AudioALSAPlaybackHandlerBase::doStereoToMonoConversionIfNeed` writes (L+R)/2 to both channels whenever `MTK_AUDIO_NUMBER_OF_SPEAKER` is 1. Patching it out alone: still mono. | | Aurisys on the audio DSP, `smartpa_awinic` | **Folds to mono** | Awinic's speaker protection has one speaker model (`AW_DSP.bin`: five presets, each one 11,244-byte block for one speaker, all carrying 0.5/0.5 weights). With it replaced by MediaTek's pass-through `aurisys_demo` as well, the right slot went **silent** and the left slot still played. | | AFE routing | Yes | `I2SOUT4_CH2 <- DL_24CH_CH2` is live during playback. | | Awinic amp (`aw882xx`) | Yes | I2S slot select is register `0x06` bits 11:10 (`01` left, `10` right, `11` mono (L+R)/2), writable through the driver's `reg` attribute. Stock is left (`0x34e8`); on the right slot, cutting `I2SOUT4_CH2` silences the speaker. | | Earpiece | Left channel | `RCV <- ADDA_DL_CH1 <- DL_24CH_CH1`; `ADDA_DL_CH1` has no CH2 source. | A kernel never mattered: the routing, the amp driver, the HAL and the DSP libraries are all vendor code. Setting `MTK_AUDIO_NUMBER_OF_SPEAKER` to 2 was rejected: it also switches the HAL to a `dual_speaker_output` path that does not exist in this phone's `audio_device.xml`, and puts Awinic's protection into two-amp mode with one amp fitted. ## Mono and stereo **Checksums**: every release lists the SHA-256 of its files, in the description and in `SHA256SUMS.txt`. **Test files**: every release carries `LEFT_ONLY_3min.wav` (left channel only) and `LEFT10s_RIGHT10s.wav` (spoken "left" / "right", then 10 s from that side only), built by `tools/make-test-audio.py`. In Stereo the left-only file plays from the earpiece alone, or the speaker alone when the phone is turned with the earpiece on your right; in Mono from both. ```sh stereoctl channels # what is running, and what is staged stereoctl channels stereo # switch to stereo now stereoctl channels mono # back to stock now ``` The CMF Stereo Manager app has the same switch. **Switching without a reboot** (v0.9.4). The module restarts the audio HAL (`setprop ctl.restart vendor.audio-hal`) on the wanted files instead of rebooting: about a second of silence, players pause, calls are unaffected (measured on the CMF Phone 1). Magisk bind-mounts each of the module's files over its vendor path at boot, in init's mount namespace, which the HAL shares (measured). A live switch takes those mounts of ours off (only ours: a mount from anywhere else on those paths and the switch is refused) and mounts what the wanted mode still needs: the staged files for stereo, nothing for mono, or, where Magisk left a placeholder rather than the stock file, a copy of the phone's own stock files (copied when it booted mono, or rebuilt from the stereo files by putting the original bytes back, and kept only when it hashes to the stock build). Every file is read back through `/proc/1/root` and must hash to the expected build; the new HAL process must still be running 3 s later. If any check fails, or a call is active, the mounts are undone and the change waits for a reboot. **What stereo changes**, and nothing else: 1. **The HAL fold**: `doStereoToMonoConversionIfNeed` no longer folds to mono, and the DSP task is told the speaker is stereo (`hw_info` bit `0x4`, two branches). Since v0.9.5 that function instead does the **orientation swap** (below). 222 bytes in four places; the result must hash to the tested build. 2. **The DSP fold**: `AURISYS_SCENARIO_DSP_PLAYBACK_SMARTPA` runs `aurisys_demo` instead of `smartpa_awinic`. The phone's own `aurisys_config_rv.xml` already declares `aurisys_demo` for that scenario (2 channels in/out, IV reference), so this is a configuration the vendor file provides. **Calls keep `smartpa_awinic`** (`DSP_CALL_FINAL` is untouched). 3. **The amp slot**: while the earpiece plays, the daemon puts the amp on the right slot; whenever the earpiece is not playing, on mono (L+R)/2, so the speaker never plays one channel alone. The driver resets the slot on every stream start, so the first second or two of a stream is the stock left slot until the daemon's next cycle. 4. **Attenuation**: the amp is held at least `STEREO_ATTEN_DB` (default 6 dB) down through its own volume control, `aw_dev_0_volume` (1/8 dB steps, per the aw882xx driver). Mono gives the amp its previous value back. **No vendor file ships in this module.** Staging copies this phone's own `audio.primary.mt6878.so`, `audio.primary.mediatek.so` and `aurisys_config_rv.xml`, checks their SHA-256 against the analysed build, patches them, and checks the result against the tested one before putting it in the module's overlay with the original SELinux labels. Anything else — another firmware, a different file — is refused and the phone stays on mono. After a Nothing OS update the hashes will differ and stereo will refuse until the new build has been checked. **Risks, plainly:** - Awinic's processing is what keeps the speaker within its excursion and temperature limits at high volume. In stereo, media gets only the amp's hardware over-temperature / over-current cut-outs plus the attenuation. Use mono for loud listening, raise `STEREO_ATTEN_DB` if you play loud in stereo, and back off at the first distortion. - The earpiece has no protection in either mode (that was already true). - Two failed boots with the stereo overlay in place remove it and set `CHANNELS=mono` — the same watchdog the audio-policy overlay has. - With the daemon stopped (`stereoctl off`) the amp goes back to its stock left slot on the next stream, so in stereo the speaker would play the left channel alone. Switch to mono if you want the module off. - **Orientation swap** (v0.9.5): turned with the earpiece on your right, left and right swap so the image stays the right way round. The earpiece cannot be routed to the right channel (its DAC input has no CH2 source), so the swap is done in the stream itself, in the HAL: Android already sends the HAL the screen rotation (`rotation=0|90|270`, measured; 270 = earpiece on the right), which the stock HAL drops. The patch keeps it in `vendor.audiohal.cmf_rotation` (a MediaTek audio-HAL property, writable by the HAL under the phone's own SELinux rules) and, for the speaker-only route in 16- or 32-bit PCM (the cases MediaTek's fold handled), swaps the two channels of every buffer while it reads 270. Headphones and every other route are never touched, and neither is the primary output: Nothing's Dirac sits there and already swaps it with the rotation (measured), so swapping it again would cancel Dirac's. The code is `hal-swap/patch.S`; `hal-swap/run.sh` assembles it, runs it in an ARM64 emulator against test buffers, and checks the module carries exactly those bytes. MediaTek's "2nd loudspeaker" machinery **is** present on this build, in `/vendor/etc/audio_param/`: ``` 2nd Loudspeaker Compensation Filter (2nd-ACF) 2nd Loudspeaker High/Low Pass Filter Order bes_loudness_Sep_LR_Filter bes_loudness_L_* / bes_loudness_R_* (separate L and R filter sets) ``` An earlier revision of this file claimed it was absent. That was wrong — it came from the broken BRE greps fixed in the ERE commit, which reported a clean zero for a pattern that never matched anything. Whether the feature is merely MediaTek's stock parameter template or actually wired to a second transducer on this hardware is unresolved. --- ## Commands ``` stereoctl status module, daemon, and live control values stereoctl doctor diagnose why the earpiece is silent stereoctl reset clear saved state and start clean stereoctl probe [dir] dump the audio hardware stereoctl report fold the newest probe into one shareable .txt stereoctl on | off arm / disarm (off survives a reboot) stereoctl solo | unsolo speaker off, earpiece only - for auditioning stereoctl guard on | off re-enable / bypass the speaker-follows guard stereoctl apply | revert one-shot apply / restore stereoctl restart restart the watcher daemon stereoctl log [n] tail the log stereoctl scan [pattern] search the mixer for candidate controls stereoctl ctl NAME [VALUE] read or write one mixer control stereoctl dump every control and its value stereoctl diff [seconds] snapshot the mixer, wait, show what changed stereoctl channels [mono|stereo] show / choose the speaker channels (applied at once) stereoctl xml-patch install the stereo speaker-port overlay (reboot) stereoctl xml-revert remove it (reboot) ``` `stereoctl ctl` is the one to experiment with: find a candidate with `scan`, flip it while music plays, listen to the earpiece. --- ## Config Lives in `/data/adb/cmf-stereo/`, survives module updates. | file | what | |---|---| | `stereo.conf` | behaviour: mode, poll interval, log level | | `actions.conf` | the routing itself, one action per line | | `stereo.log` | what the daemon did | | `state/` | saved original values, used to revert | `actions.conf` syntax: ``` ctl|| set an ALSA mixer control sysfs|| write to a sysfs node prop|| set a system property ``` `MODE=playback` (default) applies the routing only while something is playing. `MODE=always` keeps it on permanently — louder in theory, harder on the earpiece, and it costs idle power. `PLAYBACK_CTL` / `PLAYBACK_VALUE` decide how "audio is playing" is detected. Empty means scan `/proc/asound` for a RUNNING substream — which **misses DSP-offload playback entirely**. On the CMF Phone 1 media is offloaded, so the procfs scan never fires and `MODE=playback` would never engage while `MODE=always` worked. It is set to `dsp_music_runtime_en` = `1`, found with `stereoctl diff`: that control flips `Off` → `On` when media starts. A named control that cannot be read falls back to the procfs scan rather than reporting "never playing" forever. `GUARD_CTL` / `GUARD_VALUE` gate the routing on a mixer control's value. On the CMF Phone 1 the guard is `aw_dev_0_switch` = `Enable`: the HAL disables the speaker amp when headphones or Bluetooth take over, so the earpiece follows the speaker instead of playing to nobody. One mixer read per cycle, no `dumpsys`. ### Earpiece gain, and how loud it can get `Handset Volume` is the receiver amp's gain on the MT6369 codec. Read from the codec driver (`snd-soc-mt6369.ko`): the control's range is 0–18, and the register runs the opposite way to the dB scale ALSA advertises for it: | value | gain | |---|---| | 0 | **+8 dB** (loudest) | | 8 | 0 dB | | 18 | −10 dB | | 31 | −40 dB (the codec's mute value) | Evidence: every output reads 31 at rest; the driver's put handler treats 31 as a special case; and the HAL itself sets 0 whenever it drives the receiver. **Versions before v0.9.2 shipped 31**, believing it was the top. That made the daemon pull the earpiece down to −40 dB every cycle while the HAL kept putting it back to +8 dB — the `Handset Volume: 0 -> 31` lines repeating in the log, and an earpiece that sounded weak and uneven. The installer now corrects any value above 18 to 0. The two earlier explanations in this README (that 31 was the ceiling, then that the control barely mattered) were both wrong; recorded rather than quietly edited, because the mistake is the useful part. `ADDA_DL_GAIN`, the digital gain before the DAC, is left alone: the HAL parks it at 63311 of 65535 (−0.3 dB), and `ADDA_DL` is shared with the headphone path. The earpiece is a receiver: it will not match the speaker, and it has no protection circuit. In stereo, balance the two by turning the **speaker** down (`STEREO_ATTEN_DB`), not by pushing the earpiece. ## Why it ships empty elsewhere The mixer control names are device-specific. A wrong write is, in ascending order of regret: nothing, silence, a HAL crash, or an earpiece driven past what a receiver is built for. The earpiece has a fraction of the excursion and power handling of the main speaker and there is no protection circuit assuming you will use it for music. So: probe first, then fill in real names. When you find a working route, start its gain low and raise it a step at a time. Distortion or rattle means back off — that damage does not come back. --- ## Safety and recovery **Boot watchdog.** If two consecutive boots fail to reach `sys.boot_completed` while the policy overlay is active, `post-fs-data.sh` deletes the overlay before it can be mounted again. A bad policy costs one extra reboot instead of a trip to recovery. **XML validation.** No patched policy is installed unless it passes a structural check — balanced ``, ``, `` and `` elements, intact root tag, no stray backslashes from a bad insertion. Android has no `xmllint`, and a malformed audio policy takes `audioserver` down hard enough to loop the boot. **Manual recovery**, if you ever need it: ```sh adb wait-for-device shell # or hold vol-down for safe mode su touch /data/adb/modules/cmf_stereo/disable reboot ``` Both Magisk and KernelSU honour the `disable` file, and `post-fs-data.sh` never touches audio when the actions list is empty. --- ## Credit: the Hi-Res Audio module This module owes a real debt to [**Hi-Res Audio™** by Adinata (@Adivenxnataly)](https://github.com/adivenxnataly/Hi-ResAudio). It is the reason we knew where to look. Before finding it, "use the earpiece as a second speaker on a MediaTek phone" was a vague idea with no entry point. That module is what pointed at MediaTek's `2nd Loudspeaker` / `bes_loudness` machinery and at the earpiece `` channel mask — and working out why those particular levers *don't* pan out on the CMF Phone 1 is what led to the routing that does. Reverse-engineering a vendor audio stack and giving the result away for free is generous work, and this project started from it. Thank you. It also aims at a different goal — high-resolution output, not dual speakers — so it is worth trying on its own terms if that is what you want. ### One bug worth reporting upstream Tested against `v2.0 with aaudio_mmap`, versionCode 20000, commit `78706f5` (2025-06-12). It bootlooped a CMF Phone 1, and the cause is a small typo with large consequences. In `customize.sh`: ```sh name="Apply Same Filter Setting with 2nd Loudspeaker\/> ``` The attribute value is never closed — `name="` opens a quote, then text, then `/>`, with no closing `"`. The fix is one character: ```sh name="Apply Same Filter Setting with 2nd Loudspeaker\"\/> ``` Without it, this reaches `Playback_ParamTreeView.xml`: ```xml

Real left/right stereo on the CMF Phone 1. The earpiece becomes the left

speaker, the bottom speaker the right — no custom kernel, just root.

Download the module ·

Get the app ·

How stereo works

|---|---|

| 🔊 Stereo | Earpiece = left, speaker = right. Games, films and music finally have sides. |

| 📢 Mono | Default. Both speakers play the full mix: louder and fuller than the bottom speaker alone. |

| 📱 App | *CMF Stereo*, a clean Nothing-style app: on/off, Mono/Stereo, two 1–10 levels. |

    About

    A Magisk / KernelSU / APatch module that makes the CMF Phone 1 play media

    out of its earpiece as well as its bottom speaker — in true stereo if you

    want it.

    It has two channel modes:

  • **mono** (default, stock audio): both drivers play the same full mix —

    • louder, fuller and taller than the single bottom-firing speaker. This was

    the whole module once, back when it was called cmf-fake-stereo.

  • **stereo**: real left/right. The **earpiece plays the left channel and the

    • speaker the right**. It costs Awinic's speaker-protection processing on

    media, so the speaker amp is held at a fixed attenuation instead. See

    Mono and stereo.

    Getting stereo took finding the two places the phone folds the speaker to

    mono; the Findings section shows

    the measurements rather than asking you to take my word.

    Verified on A015 / Tetris, MT6878, Nothing OS B4.1, Android 16.

    What it does

  • **Real stereo** in stereo mode: earpiece = left channel, bottom speaker = right
  • **Mono** mode: both speakers play the full mix, with full speaker protection
  • Plays media through the earpiece alongside the speaker, automatically
  • Earpiece at the receiver amp's maximum, +8 dB (`Handset Volume 0`), the same value the HAL uses
  • Applies only while audio is playing, so the receiver is not held energised
  • Steps aside for headphones and Bluetooth
  • Restores every control it touches on stop, disarm or uninstall
  • Disarms itself if it ever causes a failed boot
  • Switch modes with `stereoctl channels mono|stereo` or the app; the stereo

    • overlay removes itself after two failed boots

    What it does not do

  • **No speaker protection on media in stereo.** Awinic's DSP processing is the

    • part that folds to mono, so stereo replaces it (see Mono and stereo).

  • **No extra volume from the main speaker.** It is untouched.
  • **Nothing on other devices out of the box.** It installs inert elsewhere and

    • ships a probe to work out that device's routing.

    Quick start

    Flash the zip (build it with ./build.sh, or grab a release), reboot, play

    something. That is the whole setup on a CMF Phone 1 — the verified routing is

    preconfigured.

    To check it is working, with audio playing:

    su
stereoctl status     # all three controls should show want= matching now=
stereoctl solo       # speaker off, earpiece only - proves it is really the earpiece
stereoctl unsolo

    For real stereo (applied at once):

    su -c stereoctl channels stereo

    If it is ever silent, stereoctl doctor walks every layer that can cause that

    and names the one responsible.

    On other devices

    It installs with an empty actions.conf and changes nothing. Run

    stereoctl probe to dump the audio hardware — ALSA topology, every mixer

    control, smart-amp drivers, HAL configs and MediaTek's AudioParam tree — then

    stereoctl report to fold it into one shareable text file. The routing for

    that device gets written into actions.conf from what the probe finds. See

    Why it ships empty elsewhere.

    ---

    How it works

    Three layers, smallest hammer first.

    1. Mixer actions (actions.conf). The real work. An ALSA mixer control

    somewhere enables the receiver output stage; on MediaTek there is usually also

    a routing control that decides which DL (downlink) stream feeds it. Setting

    those while the speaker is playing is what puts the earpiece to work next to

    the speaker.

    The audio HAL rewrites mixer controls on every route change, so a one-shot

    write does not survive the next stream start. A small daemon re-asserts the

    values every couple of seconds and — by default — only while audio is actually

    playing, so the earpiece is not left energised all day.

    Everything touched has its original value saved under

    /data/adb/cmf-stereo/state/ and restored on stop, disarm or uninstall.

    2. Audio policy overlay (stereoctl xml-patch, optional). If the policy

    declares the speaker as AUDIO_CHANNEL_OUT_MONO, the framework downmixes to

    one channel before the HAL ever sees it, and no amount of mixer work brings

    the second channel back. The patch widens only the speaker to

    stereo, in an overlay copy — the vendor partition is never written. It is

    opt-in, validated before it is installed, and reversible.

    3. What the CMF Phone 1 actually needed. Worth recording, because it was

    not any of the obvious answers and the probe is what found it.

    Media on this device never touches the internal codec. Playback runs:

    DL_24CH_CH1/CH2 ──▶ I2SOUT4_CH1/CH2 ──▶ Awinic aw_dev_0 smart PA ──▶ speaker
                                  ◀── I2SIN4 ──▶ UL3   (IV-sense feedback)

    The earpiece hangs off the internal codec's DAC (ADDA_DL), and that DAC

    normally has no source connected at all — every one of its ~20 input

    switches sits Off. So pointing RCV Mux at the receiver routes it to a

    silent wire, which is exactly what happened on the first attempt.

    The switch that matters is ADDA_DL_CH1 DL_24CH_CH1: it feeds the internal

    DAC from the same DL_24CH stream already going to the speaker amp. Turn it

    on, then open RCV Mux, and the earpiece plays.

    There is only one Awinic device (aw_dev_0), so there is no second amp

    channel to press into service — the internal codec was the only way in.

    That alone gives both drivers the same full mix: mono mode. Real stereo

    needed one more step — switching off the two places the phone folds the

    speaker to mono — which is what stereoctl channels stereo adds (see

    Findings and

    Mono and stereo).

    Findings: what this device actually does

    Where the speaker is folded to mono

    Earlier revisions of this section said both transducers were hard-wired to

    channel 1, then that a custom kernel would be needed, then that the DSP

    firmware was the limit. All three were wrong. Each stage was measured with a

    test file that has sound on the left channel only and silence on the right,

    by switching the amp to its right slot: silence there means the right channel

    really is separate.

    | Stage | Separate L/R? | Evidence |

    |---|---|---|

    | Android framework | Yes | dumpsys media.audio_flinger: speaker output is 2-channel FL/FR, *Master mono* off. The policy's speaker port is already stereo, so stereoctl xml-patch finds nothing to change. |

    | Dirac (Nothing's speaker tuning) | Not the fold | Session-0 insert effect, 2-in/2-out presets. Removing it alone changed nothing. |

    | MediaTek audio HAL (audio.primary.mt6878.so) | Folds to mono | AudioALSAPlaybackHandlerBase::doStereoToMonoConversionIfNeed writes (L+R)/2 to both channels whenever MTK_AUDIO_NUMBER_OF_SPEAKER is 1. Patching it out alone: still mono. |

    | Aurisys on the audio DSP, smartpa_awinic | Folds to mono | Awinic's speaker protection has one speaker model (AW_DSP.bin: five presets, each one 11,244-byte block for one speaker, all carrying 0.5/0.5 weights). With it replaced by MediaTek's pass-through aurisys_demo as well, the right slot went silent and the left slot still played. |

    | AFE routing | Yes | I2SOUT4_CH2 <- DL_24CH_CH2 is live during playback. |

    | Awinic amp (aw882xx) | Yes | I2S slot select is register 0x06 bits 11:10 (01 left, 10 right, 11 mono (L+R)/2), writable through the driver's reg attribute. Stock is left (0x34e8); on the right slot, cutting I2SOUT4_CH2 silences the speaker. |

    | Earpiece | Left channel | RCV <- ADDA_DL_CH1 <- DL_24CH_CH1; ADDA_DL_CH1 has no CH2 source. |

    A kernel never mattered: the routing, the amp driver, the HAL and the DSP

    libraries are all vendor code. Setting MTK_AUDIO_NUMBER_OF_SPEAKER to 2 was

    rejected: it also switches the HAL to a dual_speaker_output path that does

    not exist in this phone's audio_device.xml, and puts Awinic's protection

    into two-amp mode with one amp fitted.

    Mono and stereo

    Checksums: every release lists the SHA-256 of its files, in the description and in

    SHA256SUMS.txt.

    Test files: every release carries LEFT_ONLY_3min.wav (left channel only) and

    LEFT10s_RIGHT10s.wav (spoken "left" / "right", then 10 s from that side only), built by

    tools/make-test-audio.py. In Stereo the left-only file plays from the earpiece alone, or the

    speaker alone when the phone is turned with the earpiece on your right; in Mono from both.

    stereoctl channels            # what is running, and what is staged
stereoctl channels stereo     # switch to stereo now
stereoctl channels mono       # back to stock now

    The CMF Stereo Manager app has the same switch.

    Switching without a reboot (v0.9.4). The module restarts the audio HAL

    (setprop ctl.restart vendor.audio-hal) on the wanted files instead of

    rebooting: about a second of silence, players pause, calls are unaffected

    (measured on the CMF Phone 1). Magisk bind-mounts each of the module's files over its

    vendor path at boot, in init's mount namespace, which the HAL shares (measured).

    A live switch takes those mounts of ours off (only ours: a mount from anywhere

    else on those paths and the switch is refused) and mounts what the wanted mode

    still needs: the staged files for stereo, nothing for mono, or, where Magisk

    left a placeholder rather than the stock file, a copy of the phone's own stock

    files (copied when it booted mono, or rebuilt from the stereo files by putting

    the original bytes back, and kept only when it hashes to the stock build). Every

    file is read back through /proc/1/root and must hash to the expected build;

    the new HAL process must still be running 3 s later. If any check fails, or a

    call is active, the mounts are undone and the change waits for a reboot.

    What stereo changes, and nothing else:

  • **The HAL fold**: `doStereoToMonoConversionIfNeed` no longer folds to mono,

    • and the DSP task is told the speaker is stereo (hw_info bit 0x4, two

    branches). Since v0.9.5 that function instead does the orientation swap

    (below). 222 bytes in four places; the result must hash to the tested build.

  • **The DSP fold**: `AURISYS_SCENARIO_DSP_PLAYBACK_SMARTPA` runs

    • aurisys_demo instead of smartpa_awinic. The phone's own

    aurisys_config_rv.xml already declares aurisys_demo for that scenario

    (2 channels in/out, IV reference), so this is a configuration the vendor

    file provides. Calls keep smartpa_awinic (DSP_CALL_FINAL is

    untouched).

  • **The amp slot**: while the earpiece plays, the daemon puts the amp on the

    • right slot; whenever the earpiece is not playing, on mono (L+R)/2, so the

    speaker never plays one channel alone. The driver resets the slot on every

    stream start, so the first second or two of a stream is the stock left

    slot until the daemon's next cycle.

  • **Attenuation**: the amp is held at least `STEREO_ATTEN_DB` (default 6 dB)

    • down through its own volume control, aw_dev_0_volume (1/8 dB steps, per

    the aw882xx driver). Mono gives the amp its previous value back.

    No vendor file ships in this module. Staging copies this phone's own

    audio.primary.mt6878.so, audio.primary.mediatek.so and

    aurisys_config_rv.xml, checks their SHA-256 against the analysed build,

    patches them, and checks the result against the tested one before putting it

    in the module's overlay with the original SELinux labels. Anything else —

    another firmware, a different file — is refused and the phone stays on mono.

    After a Nothing OS update the hashes will differ and stereo will refuse until

    the new build has been checked.

    Risks, plainly:

  • Awinic's processing is what keeps the speaker within its excursion and

    • temperature limits at high volume. In stereo, media gets only the amp's

    hardware over-temperature / over-current cut-outs plus the attenuation. Use

    mono for loud listening, raise STEREO_ATTEN_DB if you play loud in

    stereo, and back off at the first distortion.

  • The earpiece has no protection in either mode (that was already true).
  • Two failed boots with the stereo overlay in place remove it and set

    • CHANNELS=mono — the same watchdog the audio-policy overlay has.

  • With the daemon stopped (`stereoctl off`) the amp goes back to its stock

    • left slot on the next stream, so in stereo the speaker would play the left

    channel alone. Switch to mono if you want the module off.

  • **Orientation swap** (v0.9.5): turned with the earpiece on your right, left

    • and right swap so the image stays the right way round. The earpiece cannot be

    routed to the right channel (its DAC input has no CH2 source), so the swap is

    done in the stream itself, in the HAL: Android already sends the HAL the

    screen rotation (rotation=0|90|270, measured; 270 = earpiece on the right),

    which the stock HAL drops. The patch keeps it in

    vendor.audiohal.cmf_rotation (a MediaTek audio-HAL property, writable by

    the HAL under the phone's own SELinux rules) and, for the speaker-only route

    in 16- or 32-bit PCM (the cases MediaTek's fold handled), swaps the two

    channels of every buffer while it reads 270. Headphones and every other

    route are never touched, and neither is the primary output: Nothing's Dirac

    sits there and already swaps it with the rotation (measured), so swapping it

    again would cancel Dirac's. The code is hal-swap/patch.S; hal-swap/run.sh

    assembles it, runs it in an ARM64 emulator against test buffers, and checks

    the module carries exactly those bytes.

    MediaTek's "2nd loudspeaker" machinery is present on this build, in

    /vendor/etc/audio_param/:

    2nd Loudspeaker Compensation Filter (2nd-ACF)
2nd Loudspeaker High/Low Pass Filter Order
bes_loudness_Sep_LR_Filter
bes_loudness_L_*  /  bes_loudness_R_*   (separate L and R filter sets)

    An earlier revision of this file claimed it was absent. That was wrong — it

    came from the broken BRE greps fixed in the ERE commit, which reported a

    clean zero for a pattern that never matched anything. Whether the feature is

    merely MediaTek's stock parameter template or actually wired to a second

    transducer on this hardware is unresolved.

    Config

    Lives in /data/adb/cmf-stereo/, survives module updates.

    | file | what |

    |---|---|

    | stereo.conf | behaviour: mode, poll interval, log level |

    | actions.conf | the routing itself, one action per line |

    | stereo.log | what the daemon did |

    | state/ | saved original values, used to revert |

    actions.conf syntax:

    ctl|<mixer control name>|<value>     set an ALSA mixer control
sysfs|<path>|<value>                 write to a sysfs node
prop|<property>|<value>              set a system property

    MODE=playback (default) applies the routing only while something is playing.

    MODE=always keeps it on permanently — louder in theory, harder on the

    earpiece, and it costs idle power.

    PLAYBACK_CTL / PLAYBACK_VALUE decide how "audio is playing" is detected.

    Empty means scan /proc/asound for a RUNNING substream — which **misses

    DSP-offload playback entirely**. On the CMF Phone 1 media is offloaded, so the

    procfs scan never fires and MODE=playback would never engage while

    MODE=always worked. It is set to dsp_music_runtime_en = 1, found with

    stereoctl diff: that control flips Off → On when media starts. A named

    control that cannot be read falls back to the procfs scan rather than

    reporting "never playing" forever.

    GUARD_CTL / GUARD_VALUE gate the routing on a mixer control's value. On

    the CMF Phone 1 the guard is aw_dev_0_switch = Enable: the HAL disables

    the speaker amp when headphones or Bluetooth take over, so the earpiece

    follows the speaker instead of playing to nobody. One mixer read per cycle,

    no dumpsys.

    Earpiece gain, and how loud it can get

    Handset Volume is the receiver amp's gain on the MT6369 codec. Read from the

    codec driver (snd-soc-mt6369.ko): the control's range is 0–18, and the

    register runs the opposite way to the dB scale ALSA advertises for it:

    | value | gain |

    |---|---|

    | 0 | +8 dB (loudest) |

    | 8 | 0 dB |

    | 18 | −10 dB |

    | 31 | −40 dB (the codec's mute value) |

    Evidence: every output reads 31 at rest; the driver's put handler treats 31

    as a special case; and the HAL itself sets 0 whenever it drives the receiver.

    Versions before v0.9.2 shipped 31, believing it was the top. That made

    the daemon pull the earpiece down to −40 dB every cycle while the HAL kept

    putting it back to +8 dB — the Handset Volume: 0 -> 31 lines repeating in

    the log, and an earpiece that sounded weak and uneven. The installer now

    corrects any value above 18 to 0. The two earlier explanations in this README

    (that 31 was the ceiling, then that the control barely mattered) were both

    wrong; recorded rather than quietly edited, because the mistake is the useful

    part.

    ADDA_DL_GAIN, the digital gain before the DAC, is left alone: the HAL parks

    it at 63311 of 65535 (−0.3 dB), and ADDA_DL is shared with the headphone

    path.

    The earpiece is a receiver: it will not match the speaker, and it has no

    protection circuit. In stereo, balance the two by turning the speaker down

    (STEREO_ATTEN_DB), not by pushing the earpiece.

    Why it ships empty elsewhere

    The mixer control names are device-specific. A wrong write is, in ascending

    order of regret: nothing, silence, a HAL crash, or an earpiece driven past

    what a receiver is built for. The earpiece has a fraction of the excursion and

    power handling of the main speaker and there is no protection circuit assuming

    you will use it for music.

    So: probe first, then fill in real names. When you find a working route, start

    its gain low and raise it a step at a time. Distortion or rattle means back

    off — that damage does not come back.

    ---

    Safety and recovery

    Boot watchdog. If two consecutive boots fail to reach sys.boot_completed

    while the policy overlay is active, post-fs-data.sh deletes the overlay

    before it can be mounted again. A bad policy costs one extra reboot instead of

    a trip to recovery.

    XML validation. No patched policy is installed unless it passes a

    structural check — balanced , , and

    elements, intact root tag, no stray backslashes from a bad

    insertion. Android has no xmllint, and a malformed audio policy takes

    audioserver down hard enough to loop the boot.

    Manual recovery, if you ever need it:

    adb wait-for-device shell           # or hold vol-down for safe mode
su
touch /data/adb/modules/cmf_stereo/disable
reboot

    Both Magisk and KernelSU honour the disable file, and post-fs-data.sh

    never touches audio when the actions list is empty.

    Credit: the Hi-Res Audio module

    This module owes a real debt to

    Hi-Res Audio™ by Adinata (@Adivenxnataly).

    It is the reason we knew where to look. Before finding it, "use the earpiece

    as a second speaker on a MediaTek phone" was a vague idea with no entry point.

    That module is what pointed at MediaTek's 2nd Loudspeaker / bes_loudness

    machinery and at the earpiece channel mask — and working out

    why those particular levers *don't* pan out on the CMF Phone 1 is what led to

    the routing that does. Reverse-engineering a vendor audio stack and giving the

    result away for free is generous work, and this project started from it.

    Thank you.

    It also aims at a different goal — high-resolution output, not dual speakers —

    so it is worth trying on its own terms if that is what you want.

    One bug worth reporting upstream

    Tested against v2.0 with aaudio_mmap, versionCode 20000, commit 78706f5

    (2025-06-12). It bootlooped a CMF Phone 1, and the cause is a small typo with

    large consequences. In customize.sh:

    name="Apply Same Filter Setting with 2nd Loudspeaker\/>

    The attribute value is never closed — name=" opens a quote, then text, then

    />, with no closing ". The fix is one character:

    name="Apply Same Filter Setting with 2nd Loudspeaker\"\/>

    Without it, this reaches Playback_ParamTreeView.xml:

    <Field ... name="Apply Same Filter Setting with 2nd Loudspeaker/>

    MediaTek's AudioParamParser cannot parse that, so the audio HAL aborts on

    every boot. The sed fires on any device carrying a bes_loudness_L_lpf_order

    field.

    Two other things to be aware of on a device like this one: it forces

    aaudio.mmap_policy=3 / aaudio.mmap_exclusive_policy=3 plus

    killall audioserver, which needs a HAL with an MMAP PCM path; and it sets

    the speaker channel mask to AUDIO_CHANNEL_OUT_SURROUND, which not every

    speaker port accepts.

    And a correction to an earlier version of this file, which claimed its

    insertions land mid-element: they do not. It computes the

    correct insertion point (POL + POLD - 1, the last line of the

    primary output block) and only writes when that matches a known constant,

    so placement is self-consistent, and otherwise it skips. That claim was wrong

    and is retracted.

    Why its stereo approach doesn't work on this device

    Not a criticism of the approach — it is sound on hardware that has a second

    loudspeaker. Two things stop it here (this module's stereo comes from a

    different route entirely, see Mono and stereo):

  • `Playback_ParamTreeView.xml` is the **view definition** for MediaTek's

    • parameter tuning tool (TreeRoot, Feature, FieldList,

    CategoryPathList). The runtime coefficients live in

    PlaybackACF_AudioParam.xml. Editing the view changes which fields a tuning

    application displays, not what the DSP does.

  • On the CMF Phone 1 every `bes_loudness_R_*` value and

    • bes_loudness_Sep_LR_Filter read 0x0 — MediaTek's stock template,

    untuned, because this phone has no second loudspeaker. And 2nd-ACF is a

    *filter* feature: it applies a different EQ curve to a second transducer's

    channel, it does not create a route to one.

    What this module took from it: edit the element you mean to change, validate

    the result, and keep a way back. Hence the block-aware awk, the XML

    structural check, and the boot watchdog.

    Do not run both modules at the same time — they touch the same files.

    ---

    tinymix

    Mixer controls cannot be read or written without a tinymix binary, and the

    CMF Phone 1 ships none. The module bundles one: a statically linked aarch64

    build of upstream tinyalsa, hardware backend only, no dlopen. Provenance,

    license and the exact build command are in bin/README.md.

    If you would rather not trust a shipped binary, build it yourself and drop it

    at /data/adb/cmf-stereo/bin/tinymix (chmod 0755) — that path is searched

    first. Termux's tinyalsa package works too.

    Search order: /data/adb/cmf-stereo/bin, the module's bin/, /vendor/bin,

    /system/bin, /odm/bin, /data/local/tmp, then $PATH. A vendor-supplied

    tinymix wins over the bundled one. Both the tinyalsa 1.x

    tinymix NAME VALUE and the 2.x tinymix set NAME VALUE calling conventions

    are handled, detected via --help rather than by guessing from an error

    message.

    ---

    Uninstall

    Remove it in your root manager. uninstall.sh stops the daemon and restores

    every control it touched. /data/adb/cmf-stereo/ is left in place so a

    reinstall does not lose your routing; delete it by hand for a clean slate.

    ---

    Development

    tests/run-tests.sh exercises the parts that do not need a phone — the action

    engine's save/apply/revert cycle, the boot watchdog, the XML structural

    validator, and the speaker-port rewrite (including the self-closing-element

    and no-speaker-port cases). Run it on any Linux box:

    sh tests/run-tests.sh

    ./build.sh packages the flashable zip.

    Layout:

    | path | what |

    |---|---|

    | scripts/common.sh | action engine, tinymix handling, guard, snapshots |

    | scripts/stereo-daemon.sh | applies and re-asserts the routing |

    | scripts/stereoctl | the CLI |

    | scripts/probe.sh | hardware dump |

    | scripts/xml_patch.sh | audio-policy overlay (opt-in, not for this device) |

    | config/actions.cmf1.conf | the verified CMF Phone 1 routing |

    | bin/tinymix | static aarch64 tinyalsa build, see bin/README.md |
